rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking a neck removes restraint; freeing a slave removes the condition of bondage, like releasing a pledge or loosening a fetter.
rows.anchor: الفك فرق يزيل المنع كفك القيد والغل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the verbal noun is fakkākan with fatḥa on its first letter, not kasra.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : في «المصادر » فكها يفكها فكاكا بفتح الفاء في المصدر ولا تقل بكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs customarily bound captives by neck and hands; release came to be called fakkāk even when the captive had not been bound.
rows.anchor: كانت عادة العرب في الأسارى شد رقابهم وأيديهم فجرى ذلك فيهم وإن لم يشدد

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhṭal's line uses freeing fetters as poetic evidence for the sense of liberation.
rows.anchor: قال الأخطل : أبني كليب إن عمى اللذا *** قتلا الملوك وفككا الأغلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One way to free a neck is to emancipate a slave directly.
rows.anchor: فك الرقبة قد يكون بأن يعتق الرجل رقبة من الرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may also help a contracted slave pay the sum required to buy his own freedom.
rows.anchor: بأن يعطي مكاتبا ما يصرفه إلى جهة فكاك نفسه

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: A report from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib says the Prophet distinguished freeing someone outright from contributing toward that person's purchase price.
rows.anchor: روى البراء بن عازب ، قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that a person frees his own neck through worship that earns Paradise, the greater freedom from the Fire.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد أن يفك المرء رقبة نفسه بما يتكلفه من العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading treats the phrase as an implied nominal predicate, emancipation or feeding; another reads the verbs فك رقبة أو أطعم as a substitute for اقتحم العقبة.
rows.anchor: قرئ { فك رقبة } أو إطعام ، والتقدير هي فك رقبة أو إطعام وقرئ : { فك رقبة أو أطعم }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers the verbal reading because فك and أطعم are verbs coordinated with كان; a nominal conjunction would fit if the wording were ثم إن كان.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : وهو أشبه الوجهين بصحيح العربية لقوله : { ثم كان } لأن فك وأطعم فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase وما أدراك ما العقبة is an intervening parenthesis.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وما أدراك ما العقبة } اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds emancipation to be the best form of charity, while his two companions prefer almsgiving; the verse favors Abū Ḥanīfa by mentioning emancipation first.
rows.anchor: عند أبي حنيفة العتق أفضل أنواع الصدقات ، وعند صاحبيه الصدقة أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who overcomes the obstacle must be among the believers; without faith the acts of obedience bring no benefit and do not constitute a successful crossing.
rows.anchor: فإنه إن لم يكن منهم لم ينتفع بشيء من هذه الطاعات ، ولا مقتحما للعقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that ثم delays the mention of faith, not its existence; the cited verse means to mention the father's prior eminence afterward.
rows.anchor: أن هذا التراخي في الذكر لا في الوجود ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line illustrates that ثم can order mention rather than events: the father and grandfather had already attained eminence before the person named first.
rows.anchor: إن من ساد ثم ساد أبوه *** ثم قد ساد قبل ذلك جده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation places faith at the end of the person's life: dying in faith is a condition for receiving the benefit of deeds.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد ، ثم كان في عاقبة أمره من الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some hold that deeds done devotionally before belief in Muhammad can still be rewarded if their doer later believes in him.
rows.anchor: فعند بعضهم أنه يثاب على تلك الطاعات

rows.speaker: حكيم بن حزام
rows.claim: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām asked the Prophet about good deeds from the pre-Islamic period, and the Prophet replied that he had embraced Islam with the good he had already done.
rows.anchor: أن حكيم بن حزام بعدما أسلم قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إنا كنا نأتي بأعمال الخير في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth explanation takes ثم as ranking faith later in merit: its reward far exceeds the reward for the other deeds.
rows.anchor: تراخي الإيمان وتباعده في الرتبة والفضيلة عن العنق والصدقة لأن درجة ثواب الإيمان أعظم بكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exhorting one another to patience includes steadfastness in faith, restraint from sins, perseverance in worship, and endurance of believers' trials.
rows.anchor: يوصي بعضهم بعضا بالصبر على الإيمان والثبات عليه أو الصبر على المعاصي وعلى الطاعات والمحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual exhortation to mercy means urging compassion for the oppressed and poor, and restraining someone approaching a wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أن يحث بعضهم بعضا على أن يرحم المظلوم أو الفقير ، أو يرحم المقدم على منكر فيمنعه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that a person must guide others toward truth and, as far as possible, stop them from following evil and falsehood.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنه يجب على المرء أن يدل غيره على طريق الحق ويمنعه من سلوك طريق الشر والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as overcoming the obstacle are the foremost Companions, including the four caliphs, known for steadfastness in religion and mercy toward people.
rows.anchor: أكابر الصحابة كالخلفاء الأربعة وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience expresses honoring God's command, while mercy expresses compassion for God's creatures; together they encompass the foundations of obedience.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى التعظيم لأمر الله

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some investigators describe the foundations of Sufism as sincerity with God and good character with people.
rows.anchor: إن الأصل في التصوف أمران : صدق مع الحق ؟ وخلق مع الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first preceding interpretation, the exception is disconnected: rather, righteous elderly people receive lasting reward for obedience, patience in God's trial of aging, endured hardship, and worship despite weakened movement.
rows.anchor: على القول الأول منقطع ، والمعنى ولكن الذين كانوا صالحين من الهرمى فلهم ثواب دائم على طاعتهم وصبرهم على ابتلاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second preceding interpretation, the exception is straightforwardly connected.
rows.anchor: وأما على القول الثاني فالاستثناء متصل ظاهر الاتصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of غير ممنون is that the reward is neither diminished nor cut off.
rows.anchor: غير منقوص ولا مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that no one reminds the recipients of the reward as a favor.
rows.anchor: لا يمن به عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings describe the reward: it must endure without interruption and remain free from the humiliation of reproach.
rows.anchor: لأنه يجب أن يكون غير منقطع وأن لا يكون منغصا بالمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On describing the Resurrection, God divides people into two groups according to the heaviness or lightness of their scales.
rows.anchor: لما وصف يوم القيامة قسم الناس فيه إلى قسمين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes mawāzīn as the plural of mawzūn, meaning a deed with weight and worth before God; he compares it to saying one thing is by the measure or weight of another.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء قال : ونظيره يقال : عندي درهم بميزان درهمك ووزن درهمك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the word as balances with a tongue and two pans: obedient people's good deeds appear beautiful and, if they outweigh, lead to Paradise; unbelievers' evil deeds appear ugly and light, leading to the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الميزان له لسان وكفتان لا يوزن فيه إلا الأعمال فيؤتى بحسنات المطيع في أحسن صورة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the balance has two pans but does not describe it further.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : في الميزان له كفتان ولا يوصف

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: The theologians say deeds themselves cannot be weighed, especially after ceasing to exist; instead, records may be weighed, light and darkness may signify good and evil, or the records may be embodied beautifully or hideously, publicly revealing people's standing.
rows.anchor: قال المتكلمون : إن نفس الحسنات والسيئات لا يصح وزنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĪsha is a verbal noun meaning living or life, just as khīfa means fear.
rows.anchor: فالعيشة مصدر بمعنى العيش ، كالخيفة بمعنى الخوف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains rāḍiya as a life possessing satisfaction, one its owner approves, like labin and tāmir meaning possessing milk and dates; commentators gloss it as pleasing to its owner.
rows.anchor: فقال الزجاج : معناه أي عيشة ذات رضا يرضاها صاحبها وهي كقولهم لابن وتامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scales are light because a person's good deeds are few, so the evil deeds outweigh them.
rows.anchor: أي قلت : حسناته فرجحت السيئات على الحسنات

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr says scales are heavy when people follow truth and bear its weight in worldly life, and light when they follow falsehood and its ease; a scale containing only truth is rightly heavy, one holding falsehood rightly light.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه : إنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينه باتباعهم الحق في الدنيا وثقله عليهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says truth itself is heavy while falsehood is light.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : إنما كان كذلك لأن الحق ثقيل والباطل خفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes al-Hāwiya as a name for the deep Fire into which its inhabitants plunge far below; the verse then means that the Fire is the person's abode.
rows.anchor: أن الهاوية من أسماء النار وكأنها النار العميقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling an abode a person's mother is a comparison: when afraid, a child turns to its mother for refuge.
rows.anchor: للمأوى أم على سبيل التشبيه بالأم التي لا يقع الفزع

rows.speaker: الأخفش والكلبي وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash, al-Kalbī, and Qatāda say the person's head is his mother in the Fire, because people fall into it headfirst.
rows.anchor: ذكره الأخفش ، والكلبي ، وقتادة قال : لأنهم يهوون في النار على رؤوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view explains the phrase through an Arab curse wishing someone's mother to fall: when he falls and dies, she falls in grief, so the verse means that the person is destroyed.
rows.anchor: إذا دعوا على الرجل بالهلاك قالوا : هوت أمه لأنه إذا هوى أي سقط وهلك فقد هوت أمه حزنا وثكلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihlāʾ means turning someone toward amusement; amusement follows desire, and turning to one thing entails turning away from another.
rows.anchor: المسألة الأولى : الإلهاء الصرف إلى اللهو . واللهو الانصراف إلى ما يدعو إليه الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary Arabic, a person who says something distracted him means that it made him forget and occupied him.
rows.anchor: ألهاني فلان عن كذا أي أنساني وشغلني

rows.speaker: الزبير
rows.claim: A report says al-Zubayr would leave his conversation when he heard thunder; the phrase لهى عن حديثه means he abandoned and turned away from it.
rows.anchor: أن الزبير كان إذا سمع صوت الرعد لهى عن حديثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takāthur is boasting against others about abundance in wealth, status, and distinctions.
rows.anchor: والتكاثر التباهي بكثرة المال والجاه والمناقب

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim notes that the reciprocal pattern tafāʿul can express an exchange between two people, a deliberate effort to do something, or an action occurring intransitively.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : التكاثر تفاعل عن الكثرة والتفاعل يقع على أحد وجوه ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may describe reciprocal rivalry, each person claiming more wealth and followers, or strenuous efforts by the ambitious to keep multiplying wealth.
rows.anchor: ولفظ التكاثر في هذه الآية ويحتمل الوجهين الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī treats takāthur and tafākhur as synonymous and links the verse to the wording وتفاخر بينكم.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن التفاخر والتكاثر شيء واحد ونظير هذه الآية قوله تعالى : { وتفاخر بينكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People boast about three ranks of felicity: the inward soul, the body, and what surrounds the body; inward felicity includes knowledge and virtuous character, bodily felicity includes health and beauty, and external goods include wealth, status, relatives, and friends.
rows.anchor: وأجناس السعادة ثلاثة : ( فأحدها ) : في النفس ( والثانية ) : في البدن ( والثالثة ) : فيما يطيف بالبدن من خارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer attributed to Abraham for wisdom and joining the righteous exemplifies inward knowledge and virtue, through which enduring spiritual happiness is gained.
rows.anchor: وهما المرادان بقوله حكاية عن إبراهيم : { رب هب لي حكما وألحقني بالصالحين } وبهما ينال البقاء الأبدي والسعادة السرمدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: External goods serve the body, while bodily health is sought to make time for lasting spiritual happiness; people will even sacrifice wealth and status to relieve bodily pain.
rows.anchor: إذا تألم عضو من أعضائه فإنه يجعل المال والجاه فداء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wise person prioritizes higher felicities: boasting about wealth, status, helpers, and kin celebrates the lowest rank and diverts one from spiritual happiness through knowledge and action.
rows.anchor: فالتفاخر بالمال والجاه والأعوان والأقرباء تفاخر بأخس المراتب من أسباب السعادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemnation includes rivalry in numbers, money, status, relatives, supporters, armies, and every worldly pleasure and desire.
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيه التكاثر بالعدد وبالمال والجاه والأقرباء والأنصار والجيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألهاكم may be a statement about the audience or an interrogative rebuke, أألهاكم; Razi compares the interrogative reading with cited forms of أنذرتهم and إذا كنا عظاما.
rows.anchor: لتوبيخ والتقريع أي أألهاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns worldly rivalry, but reason shows that competition for real felicities is praiseworthy; rivalry is not blameworthy in every sense.
rows.anchor: الآية دلت على أن التكاثر والتفاخر مذموم والعقل دل على أن التكاثر والتفاخر في السعادات الحقيقية غير مذموم

rows.speaker: العباس وشيبة وعلي
rows.claim: A report recounts al-ʿAbbās boasting of control of the water supply, Shayba of the key, and ʿAlī of cutting down unbelief with his sword; their distress was followed by revelation of the verse about watering pilgrims.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك ما روي من تفاخر العباس بأن السقاية بيده ، وتفاخر شيبة بأن المفتاح بيده إلى أن قال علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says a person may mention obedience and good character when he expects others to imitate him, citing the command to speak of God's favor.
rows.anchor: أنه يجوز للإنسان أن يفتخر بطاعاته ومحاسن أخلاقه إذا كان يظن أن غيره يقتدي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rivalry in knowledge, obedience, and good character is praiseworthy and a source of good; the condemned rivalry concerns worldly goods that hinder worship.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن مطلق التكاثر ليس بمذموم ، بل التكاثر في العلم والطاعة والأخلاق الحميدة ، هو المحمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article is not generic; it points to the familiar worldly multiplication of pleasures and attachments that distracts from God's worship, a known evil across reason and religions.
rows.anchor: فالألف واللام في التكاثر ليسا للاستغراق ، بل للمعهود السابق ، وهو التكاثر في الدنيا ولذاتها وعلائقها

rows.speaker: بنو سهم وبنو عبد مناف
rows.claim: One reported occasion is a numbers contest between Banū Sahm and Banū ʿAbd Manāf: after counting living and dead members, Banū Sahm claimed the larger total.
rows.anchor: نزلت في بني سهم وبني عبد مناف تفاخروا أيهم أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi sees the grave-visiting wording as matching a past rivalry; the rebuke asks what it would profit people even if they were more numerous.
rows.anchor: لأن قوله : { حتى زرتم المقابر } يدل على أنه أمر مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visiting graves means going to a place, especially to soften the heart and remove love of worldly life; here grave-visitation perversely results from hard hearts and absorption in worldly love.
rows.anchor: وأهمها وأولاها بالرعاية ترقيق القلب

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says he had forbidden grave visits and then permits them, since visiting graves is a reminder.
rows.anchor: على ما قال عليه السلام : «كنت نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور ألا فزوروها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view identifies the rivalry as pursuit of wealth, supported by a report in which the Prophet recites the verse and explains what a person's wealth actually consists of.
rows.anchor: مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير عن أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the wealth interpretation, visiting graves is a euphemism for dying; the verse says that pursuit of wealth occupied people until death arrived.
rows.anchor: أي حتى متم وزيارة القبر عبارة عن الموت

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarīr's verse uses visiting graves to mean that Abū Mālik died, serving as poetic evidence for the euphemism.
rows.anchor: قال جرير للأخطل : زار القبور أبو مالك *** فأصبح ألأم زوارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection is that a visitor leaves after a while whereas the dead remain in their graves; Razi answers that a visitor must eventually depart and grave-dwellers likewise leave for the place of reckoning.
rows.anchor: لكن لابد له من الرحيل ، وكذا أهل القبور يرحلون عنها إلى مكان الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To explain the past tense for a future death, one possibility is that the address concerns people nearing death from old age, already standing at the brink of the grave.
rows.anchor: كان مشرفا على الموت بسبب الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer reports the fate of earlier people as admonition to their successors, treating it as though it were news of the current audience because they follow the same way.
rows.anchor: أن الخبر عمن تقدمهم وعظا لهم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says God addresses unbelievers with this sura on Judgment Day, when their visits to graves have already occurred.
rows.anchor: أبو مسلم : إن الله تعالى يتكلم بهذه السورة يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view says greed for wealth prevented people from paying financial obligations until death, when they finally bequeathed money for zakat and pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: الحرص على المال وطلب تكثيره حتى منعتم الحقوق المالية إلى حين الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth view says rivalry turns hearts to stone, leaving only the small amount of religious feeling associated with visiting graves; Razi compares this with the rebuke that people give little thanks.
rows.anchor: قلوبكم كأنها أحجار لا تنكسر البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse leaves the object of ألهاكم unstated because an absolute construction intensifies blame and lets the mind supply every possible object.
rows.anchor: المطلق أبلغ في الذم لأنه يذهب الوهم فيه كل مذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object includes neglect of remembrance, duties, recommended acts, religious knowledge, worship, reflection, and contemplation.
rows.anchor: ألهاكم التكاثر عن ذكر الله وعن الواجبات والمندوبات في المعرفة والطاعة والتفكر والتدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read against the preceding discussion of the Calamity, the verse means that worldly rivalry distracted people from contemplating it and preparing for it before death.
rows.anchor: عن التدبر في أمر القارعة والاستعداد لها قبل الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read with the following grave-visitation clause, the verse means that rivalry made people forget the grave until they actually visited it.
rows.anchor: إلى الأسفل فالمعنى ألهاكم التكاثر
